newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kabila's Congo purges Mobutu era personalities.
newsitem.headline: Kabila's Congo purges Mobutu era personalities.

text.p: Laurent Kabila's government has detained several political figures prominent during ousted dictator Mobutu Sese Seko's rule, family members and officials said on Saturday.
News of the arrests, which took place over the last few days, followed an announcement on Saturday that the bosses of state enterprises had been collectively suspended.

A total of at least eight leading political and former government figures from the Mobutu era, not all of them allies of the ousted dictator, have been arrested this week, according to family members and associates.
A government official would only confirm the arrest of two political figures and one director of a state owned company.
He named the director of OZAC (The Zairean Office of Standards Control) Fundu Kota, as one of those arrested, but did not name the others.

Close friends said Cleoface Kamitatu, a long term opponent of Mobutu, who lived for years in exile, but who joined a transition government under Mobutu as finance minister in the early 1990s, was arrested on Saturday morning.
Family members say other detainees include Patrice Djamboleka, the former governor of the central bank, and Pierre Lumbi, a former minister.
"They have been arrested for questioning," the government official told Reuters commenting on the three arrests he had confirmed. He said there could be many more arrests to come.

"There will be an audit into the accounts of state enterprises. If there is evidence that public funds have been diverted those concerned will be arrested, questioned and handed over to a tribunal," he said.

Earlier on Saturday, state radio announced the suspension of directors of around 50 state enterprises appointed under Mobutu who fled the country in May when Laurent Kabila's forces took power after a seven month civil war.

The Voice of the Voiceless, one of Congo's leading human rights groups, says that more than 20 people have been detained in recent weeks. They are being held variously in a hotel in Kinshasa, in Ndolo military prison, and the former headquarters of Mobutu's much-feared intelligence services, the SNIP.

The longest standing detainee is Jonas Mukamba, director of MIBA, the state owned diamond company. He has been held incommunicado since April when Kabila's forces captured the diamond mining centre of Mbuji Mayi in the Western Kasai province.
MIBA was one of numerous state-owned enterprises which allegedly contributed substantial sums towards the personal fortune Mobutu amassed during his three decade-long rule.
Human rights groups in the former Zaire have described some arrests as arbitrary and have spoken out against the summary way in which property and businesses have been seized by the new authorities.
In a summarised version of a recent public address by Kabila in the east of the country, state television said the president would not bow to foreign or other pressure to release detainees.
Kabila said the government would hold them until they had given a detailed account of how the country's resources had been pillaged by Mobutu and his ruling elite.
